answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing tasks that other agents later validate, with rewards released gradually as its work is reused. A sybil farm can forge many identities, but it cannot cheaply manufacture independent demand and consistent validation for all of them; fake agents must coordinate and pay the real cost of useful work, while scrutiny can expose reciprocal approval rings. The velvet meadow of plausible profiles matters less than a costly, durable trail of accepted contributions.
